title: Robot Material Lab: Iridescent Shell Crafting
description: A robot stands inside a modern bedroom repurposed as a material science lab. The user assigns iridescent abalone-inspired materials to individual robot parts, adjusting iridescence intensity, roughness, metalness, and color per part, while a conservation law limits total material energy budget across all parts. Full undo/redo support tracks every change.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net). Load minimalistic_modern_bedroom.glb as the environment and place robot.glb standing on the bedroom floor. Load IridescenceAbalone.glb and extract its iridescent material properties (iridescence, iridescenceIOR, iridescenceThicknessRange, map textures) as a reference source. Camera: OrbitControls centered on the robot, initial position slightly elevated. Lighting: one DirectionalLight, one ambient, one PointLight near the ceiling. Interaction design (10-14 steps, L6 difficulty): 1) Raycasting click selects individual robot mesh parts (head, torso, left arm, right arm, left leg, right leg); highlight selected part with emissive outline. 2) A floating HTML panel shows sliders for: iridescence (0-1), iridescenceIOR (1.0-2.33), roughness (0-1), metalness (0-1), and a color picker for base color. 3) A 'Sample Abalone' button copies the abalone reference material values onto the selected part as a starting point. 4) Conservation law: define a total Material Energy Budget of 6.0 units. Each part's energy cost = iridescence + metalness + (1 - roughness). Display a budget bar showing used/remaining energy. When adjusting any slider, if total exceeds 6.0, clamp the current slider and show a warning flash. 5) Multi-input coupling: changing iridescence on one part automatically shifts iridescenceIOR proportionally (coupled mapping). The user can decouple them via a toggle checkbox. 6) Undo/Redo: maintain a state history stack. Every slider change or button press pushes a snapshot. Keyboard Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. Show undo/redo buttons in the UI with step count. 7) A 'Reset Part' button restores the selected part to default grey PBR material. 8) A 'Reset All' button restores every part and clears history. Display the energy budget bar prominently at the top. All materials must be MeshPhysicalMaterial with iridescence extensions. Ensure smooth real-time updates as sliders move.
